title: Client retry heuristics playbook and idempotency guidelines for Python/TS/Go
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Establish a pragmatic, cross-language playbook for default retry/backoff behavior, idempotency key semantics, and streaming ergonomics for Redwood client SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Goal is to provide safe defaults for common production workloads, clear guidance for developers, and concrete examples + opt-out knobs for advanced cases.
background: We have accumulated many ad-hoc retry conventions across SDKs and services. This causes inconsistent app behavior, surprises for customers (duplicate side effects, wasted tokens), and operational confusion during incidents. This ticket synthesizes previous guidance into a single, opinionated playbook with concrete defaults and migration guidance for SDKs.
proposed_defaults: 1) Idempotency: Non-streaming mutating requests (e.g., model fine-tunes, uploads, stateful server operations) MUST accept an idempotency_key header. SDKs generate a v4 UUID by default and expose an explicit parameter to override. 2) Retry policy: Default retries = 3 attempts (initial + 2 retries) for idempotent-safe paths; 1 attempt (no retry) for non-idempotent paths unless user supplies idempotency_key. 3) Backoff: Jittered exponential backoff base=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=6s. 4) Transport errors: retryable by default (connection reset, TCP timeouts, DNS failures). 5) 5xx server errors: retryable with backoff; 429 treated as retryable with rate-limit-aware backoff (respect Retry-After header when present). 6) Client-side timeouts: SDKs set a conservative default request timeout (30s) with per-token streaming heartbeat to keep long streams alive. These defaults are exposed as a single RetryConfig object in each SDK and are overridable per-request.
retryable_error_taxonomy: Transport errors: connection reset, ECONNRESET, ENETUNREACH, timeout socket-level — retryable
Transient DNS failures: NXDOMAIN/time-limited name resolution — retryable
Rate limiting: 429 — retryable; prefer use of Retry-After when present; augment with capped backoff
Client errors (4xx other than 429): not retryable by default; surface explicit guidance for 409 conflict where idempotent retries might apply
Application-level transient errors: e.g., model warmup or capacity signals surfaced in body (code=TEMP_CAPACITY) — treat as retryable if flagged by platform
Stream interruptions: abrupt TCP close during streaming — treat as retryable with resume heuristics when supported
idempotency_key_strategy: SDKs generate a random RFC4122 v4 UUID per request by default for mutating endpoints and attach it as X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key. For request retries performed automatically by the SDK, the same idempotency key is reused across retries. For user-supplied idempotency keys, SDKs must not overwrite the key. For streaming calls that are inherently stateful (server appends), we do not auto-retry by default; instead we surface a resumable stream token in response metadata where backend supports it and provide an opt-in client 'resume_on_failure' flag that attempts to resume using the token. Guidance: document idempotency semantics per endpoint (safe/unsafe) and make explicit when server deduplication windows apply.
streaming_ergonomics_guidance: 1) Default behavior: SDKs expose a streaming iterator/async generator that yields partial chunks. If a stream is interrupted before a final 'done' marker, SDKs will by default NOT reissue the request to avoid duplicate side effects; instead they will raise a StreamInterrupted error with an attached 'partial' flag and best-effort partial payload. 2) Resume flow: when server supports resumable streams, include 'resume_token' in initial response; SDK exposes resume_on_failure and will attempt to resume up to 1 time using server resume_token. 3) Timeouts: streaming heartbeat (lightweight no-op ping) keeps long-lived streams from being closed by intermediaries. 4) Developer ergonomics: provide helper functions: stream.to_text(), stream.collect_unstable(), stream.with_retries(retry_config) to make common patterns ergonomic.
examples_snippets:
# Python: safe mutating call with explicit idempotency key
client.mutate_state(data, idempotency_key=uuid4())

# TypeScript: override retry count for a single request
await client.request('mutate', { body, retry: { max_attempts: 0 } })

// Go: streaming with resume option
stream, err := client.Stream(ctx, req, client.WithResumeOnFailure(true))
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) export a single RetryConfig and IdempotencyKey helper with docs and defaults
All mutating endpoints in the public API surface accept an optional idempotency_key param and default to SDK-generated UUID
Retry behavior implemented in all three SDKs with unit + integration tests covering transport errors, 5xx, 429 with Retry-After, and non-retryable 4xx
Streaming ergonomics implemented: StreamInterrupted error, resume_on_failure opt-in, and example snippets in the SDK repo
Confluence playbook published and linked from SDK readmes
Migration guide for customers explaining changes and opt-out knobs
implementation_notes: Python: add RetryConfig dataclass, integrate with httpx client transport; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/182
TypeScript: centralize retry logic in core fetch wrapper; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/305
Go: provide RetryPolicy + Option functional pattern and ensure context cancellation semantics preserved; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/97
Add end-to-end smoketest that simulates intermittent 502s and verifies no duplicate side effects when idempotency keys are used
Add telemetry events: retry.attempt, retry.giveup, stream.resume_attempt, stream.interrupted for Console tracing
open_questions: Should SDKs expose per-route default override tables (e.g., long-running endpoints with higher timeouts)?
How do we advertise server-side dedupe windows (expiration) to clients in a backwards-compatible way?
Do we provide a high-level convenience API that automatically chooses idempotency behavior based on endpoint metadata?
